statement: A finite category with all finite products is a preorder; if pointed it is equivalent to the terminal category. The IX finite example lacks x times x.

statement: Rectifiability on a specified shape class implies H_ab(A)=[BA,Map_L(M,W)(a,b)] naturally, hence constant-diagram test (b).

statement: For a six-object suspension poset X and a weak equivalence Y to the finite parallel-arrow category B, restriction H_ss(B) to H_ss(Y) is not surjective.
notes: All source and target categories in the b counterexample are finite; finite code verifies fundamental 2-cycle.

statement: Each higher loop identity (c) implies its associated representability (a); pointed infinity-category pullbacks/pushouts give the coherent identities; finite-poset (b) does not force both adjoint operations.
depends_on: Parts B-C comparison when using manuscript paths
notes: Complete argument and source/finite checks stated in sections/D.tex.

statement: Cisinski finite derivable categories rectify finite inverse/direct shapes; full ABC categories and suitably complete Quillen model categories rectify all shapes in their universe.
notes: No functorial factorization, combinatoriality, or simplicial model enrichment is assumed; infinite ABC axioms are retained.

statement: Initial object, pushouts, two out of three, and enough intrinsic cofibrations imply CF1-CF4 and rectification at finite direct categories; no finite-poset counterexample under those hypotheses.
notes: All objects cofibrant and two out of six are not silently assumed; the finite theorem uses Cisinski convention.

statement: The diamond lattice has enough intrinsic cofibrations but noncofibrant objects; finite sets with isomorphisms show CF5 and CF6 do not follow from the finite axioms.
notes: FiniteSet failure of infinite axioms does not itself imply failure of rectification.

statement: Rectification at all cubes does not imply finite-poset rectification: the six-element circle face poset with every arrow weak misses degree two at its own shape.
notes: Complete argument and source/finite checks stated in sections/D.tex.

statement: Finite simplicial sets rectify finite posets but fail at BZ because strict finite automorphisms have finite order and a Nielsen monodromy has infinite order. The opposite is BK-fibrant with the same failure.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Part D(3) finite posets versus BZ and BK question
notes: BK counterexample refutes all-small-shape sufficiency, not a finite-only sufficiency statement.

statement: The nine-vertex contractible fence with all arrows weak rectifies all shapes but fails BK fibrancy through an explicit unfillable inner horn in Ex squared of its nerve.
notes: Complete argument and source/finite checks stated in sections/D.tex.

statement: A relative poset localization of an ordinary category need not rectify: finite circle P presents BZ; explicit countable signed-face orbit poset Q presents BC2 and fails rectification at the finite category BC2.
notes: Both finite P/BZ and explicit infinite Q/finite BC2 examples given; all finite target laws checked.

statement: Audit of Kaledin v3 shapes, definitions, representation and extension scope: Pos is finite chain dimension, Pos+ left-bounded, Pos+- left-finite; finite posets alone are not his base.

statement: The naive family on Kaledin Pos (respectively Pos+) is enhanced iff its canonical comparisons to coherent L(M,W) diagram categories are equivalences; the representing infinity-category is L(M,W), by Kaledin plus localization universality.
notes: Known label honours Kaledin; formal identification proof supplied, dependent on the preprint theorem. Enhanced morphisms are cartesian (7.2.2.1), with no exactness requirement.

statement: The circle relative poset fails additivity at the countably infinite discrete poset because finite zigzags yield bounded winding sequences; the finite IX category with W identities fails no enhancement axiom.
notes: Complete argument and source/finite checks stated in sections/D.tex.

statement: Later Grothendieck Cof0-Cof3 and quillenisable classes imply finite-direct rectification; full Cof4 implies ABC and all-relative-universe rectification and homotopy left Kan extensions. Filtered-colimit stability of W upgrades intrinsic cofibrations.

notes: No all-shape claim from finite completion or functorial factorization alone. Full filtered-colimit existence is part of Cof4.

statement: Accessible fundamental localizers on Cat admit left proper Thomason models and rectify all relative-small shapes; enough intrinsic fibrations is a stricter properness condition. Pointed tests are applied to pointed objects.
notes: Raw Cat is not pointed; a and c are correctly applied in pointed model category.
